articles.headline: Premier League live updates: All eyes on Anfield for Liverpool vs. Man City
articles.description: Man City's first match since being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules comes against Liverpool at Anfield. But before that, two other games are underway.
articles.body:
After a two-week international break, European club soccer is back this weekend!

We continue our Premier League coverage with two early matches, as Crystal Palace host Nottingham Forest and Hull City take on Everton.

Later, all eyes turn to Anfield for a blockbuster clash between Liverpool and Manchester City. The title contenders face off in a highly anticipated clash, with City entering the match just weeks after they were found guilty on more than 100 charges of serious breaches of Premier League financial regulations.

Elsewhere across the continent, Sassuolo host AC Milan in Serie A.

Enjoy all the updates from Sunday's matches.

articles.headline: Roberto De Zerbi sees something to build on from Tottenham draw at Man United
articles.description: Tottenham's wait for a first Premier League win of the season continues but Roberto De Zerbi takes his side to Spain for a training camp having seen promising signs in the late draw at Manchester United.
articles.body:
Tottenham's wait for a first Premier League win of the season continues but Roberto De Zerbi takes his side to Spain for a training camp having seen promising signs in the late draw at Manchester United.

A big-spending summer after scraping survival last term has increased expectations in north London, but Spurs remain without a victory after six matches.

Tottenham have only previously managed that in 1955-56 and 2008-09, but there was a sense of positivity around fans, staff and players after the latest fixture in that run.

Spurs fought back from Bryan Mbeumo firing United ahead and a Rodrigo Bentancur red card to snatch a 1-1 draw on Saturday night, when skipper Dominic Solanke headed home in stoppage time.

"We showed the right reaction. We played a great game," boss De Zerbi said.

"I think we are playing well, not [just] today, also the other games before Manchester, but today has been the game where for the first time in this season we showed to be a team.

"We played for the teammates, we played together, we believed until the end of the game, we stayed inside of the game in every situation, and we attacked as a team, we defended as a team, the right football behaviour."

Tottenham will have the chance to build on that during a training camp in Spain ahead of their return to action at home to promoted Coventry next Monday.

"To work together, to stay together, to go for dinner together, to know better each other, because to be a team you have to know the teammates, to stay together," De Zerbi said of the benefits of the trip.

- De Zerbi: I 'kissed' Rodrigo Bentancur after red card, the 'character' that Spurs need

- Senne Lammens: Man United must get 'sour' taste of late Tottenham woe out of mouth

- Michael Carrick 'hurt' by boos as Man United fall to worst start in 40 years

"We have to build the team. Now the target is to build the team, not the group of the players.

"We are a great group of players, but we are not a team yet. Today, this game, we show to be a team.

"To be a team is to play for the teammates, suffer together, attack together, defend together, the players who come inside five minutes, three minutes, like Mateus Fernandes, they have to play like they are in the first XI, without problems, without other faults.

"We have to find the balance between the confidence in ourselves and to be hungry in the training and in the games."

articles.headline: Senne Lammens: Man United must get 'sour' taste of late Tottenham woe out of mouth
articles.description: Senne Lammens has said that Manchester United head to Atlético Madrid determined to get rid of the "sour" taste left in their mouth by Saturday's draw against Tottenham.
articles.body:
Senne Lammens has said that Manchester United head to Atlético Madrid determined to get rid of the "sour" taste left in their mouth by Saturday's disappointing late draw against Tottenham.

The scrutiny on boss Michael Carrick's position and the club grows by the match with the afterglow of last season's third-place finish and Champions League return long since extinguished.

Boos rang around Old Trafford after United blew a much-needed win on Saturday night, with Spurs recovering from Rodrigo Bentancur's red card as Dominic Solanke snatched a 1-1 draw in stoppage time.

Bryan Mbeumo's fine goal had put Carrick's side on course for victory and goalkeeper Lammens said: "It's very disappointing because you find a way to get the game, to get the advantage, to score a goal, to get 1-0 up against 10 men.

"That's the position you want to be in, so it's very disappointing to get the last goal against us at the end.

"We need to learn from it a lot, because these are the games you have to try to pull towards yourself.

"To win these games is very important if you want to get a good season, so it's very important for us to learn from this and to move on, to get these games behind us."

United have just six points to show from their opening six games -- their worst start to a campaign since 1986 -- and now face a tough Champions League game at Atletico Madrid on Tuesday.

An intense Premier League trip to rivals Leeds follows on Sunday before another European game away to Como as a tough schedule rumbles on.

"I mean, you can look at it both ways, to be honest," Lammens said. "We know there are a lot of games coming very fast.

"After a disappointment, you can take that disappointment with you, or you can get it changed real quick and know there's a game coming up very quickly.

"For me personally, if I maybe don't have the best game, I'm looking forward to the next game to get that sour feeling out of my mouth, so I think that's the feeling we have to get.

"We know we showed a lot of good things as well today, so take those things and learn from the bad things. There are a lot of very important games, but we also love to play those games.

"We fought last year to be in the Champions League, so we're very happy to be there. And if you want to go far in that competition as well, you have to win those games as well."

articles.headline: Manchester City charges: Features, explainers, what's next after guilty verdict
articles.description: ESPN has you covered with everything you need to know about the latest in the Manchester City scandal.
articles.body:
After an investigation spanning years, Manchester City were found guilty on more than 100 charges of serious breaches of Premier League financial regulations. The decision is a major development in one of the biggest scandals in soccer history, but the saga is far from over.

What happens next? What does the ruling mean for England's dominant force over the past decade, its fans and its players? ESPN's writers have you covered on every angle, from transfer implications to the mood at City's rival clubs.

Check back here for the latest as this story continues to unfold.

Lindop: Was epic Man City-Liverpool rivalry all a sham after cheating scandal?

Under Jürgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola, Liverpool and Man City pushed the Premier League's standards higher than ever. But was it all a sham?

Dawson: 'We're Not Really Here': As Man City sanctions loom, it's the fans who suffer

Manchester City's financial malfeasance could send the club back down the football pyramid, a place where fans of a certain age are very familiar.

Olley: Arsenal fight back to win as Premier League resumes under cloud of Man City verdict

Does Arsenal's comeback win over Leeds close the gap on leaders Man City, or extend their own lead at the top? This is the perpetual uncertainty that hangs over the Premier League now.

Ogden: What's next for Man City? Appeals, possible punishments, how long it could take

Man City have appealed the Premier League's guilty verdict, while the sanctions board also begins its work on figuring out appropriate punishments. So what happens next, and what is the possible timeline?

It's worth reminding ourselves that the Manchester City case, which has rocked English football to its foundation, would never have seen the light of day without a spiky-haired college dropout turned self-taught hacker named Rui Pinto.

articles.headline: Jordan Henderson reveals special free-kick practice with Chelsea during international break
articles.description: Jordan Henderson revealed he pulled rank to score the first direct free-kick of his career after practicing them over the international break.
articles.body:
Jordan Henderson revealed he pulled rank to score the first direct free-kick of his career after practicing them over the international break.

Henderson, 36, used the three-week hiatus to work on his shooting with Blues set-piece coach Austin MacPhee.

It certainly paid off for the former Liverpool captain, who stepped up ahead of Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers to curl in Chelsea's fifth goal in their 5-1 demolition of Bournemouth.

"Some of the lads, and Austin, have a little bit of confidence in me, so when I have some confidence in me, I can step up and take it," Henderson told the club website.

"But we've been working on it in training for the past week or two, to be fair, and I was pretty consistent.

"Austin said 'that's what we're doing'. Morgs wasn't too happy. Cole said 'which corner are we celebrating in'.

"It was nice because it was something that we worked on and we executed it really well. So I was thankful to Cole and Morgs to let me have it."

It was a spectacular home debut for Henderson, who had scored two goals in his previous four seasons yet grabbed two in 70 minutes against the Cherries.

His first came after just 65 seconds, a 20-yard drive which flew in off a post.

Moments later Rogers made it two and João Pedro added a third 40 seconds into the second half.

Even when Evanilson reduced the arrears Chelsea kept their foot on the pedal, with Pedro grabbing another before Henderson produced his party piece.

The attacking triumvirate of Palmer, Rogers and Pedro ran Bournemouth ragged and Henderson added: "They're fantastic players, with huge talent, of course.

- Jordan Henderson, 36, nets unlikely brace as Chelsea thrash Bournemouth

- Brighton keep pressure on Man City, Arsenal with 2-0 Sunderland win

- Chelsea's Cole Palmer signs new contract until 2034

"What I was most pleased with was the work we did and the defensive attitude without the ball.

"That helps the team and gives us a platform. When we win it back, they're so good on the transition. They can kill any team with the skill, the pace, the power, and they're clinical in front of goal.

"I know everyone will speak about the goals and that's what everyone wants to see, of course, but for me I thought they worked outstandingly hard for the team and that's what I'm most impressed with."

articles.headline: Kings lose Maxime Raynaud to apparent serious knee injury
articles.description: Kings second-year center Maxime Raynaud suffered what appeared to be a serious right knee injury in Saturday's preseason game against the Warriors.
articles.headlineJa: キングス、マキシム・レイノーが深刻な膝の負傷に見舞われる
articles.descriptionJa: キングスの2年目センター、マキシム・レイノーが土曜日のウォリアーズとのプレシーズンゲーム中に、右膝の深刻な負傷と思われる症状に見舞われました。
articles.body:
The Sacramento Kings lost second-year center Maxime Raynaud after what appeared to be a serious right knee injury late in the first half of their preseason game at the Golden State Warriors on Saturday night.

Raynaud was setting a screen for rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr. with Golden State's Stephen Curry in the vicinity defending it. As bodies collided, Raynaud took contact to the outside of his right knee, immediately yelling in pain and crumpling to the floor.

The seriousness of the situation became obvious quickly. Sacramento coach Doug Christie called timeout and walked out to the middle of the floor to check on Raynaud, who had his hands over his face. As teammates descended, team trainers called over the EMT with a wheelchair to help Raynaud to the locker room.

Raynaud spent halftime getting tests on the injury in Chase Center. The team officially ruled him out with a right knee injury early in the third quarter.

At that time, a dispirited Raynaud was wheeled from the X-ray room back to the area outside the visitors locker room. While there, Kings general manager Scott Perry and team owner Vivek Ranadive visited him. Ranadive gave Raynaud a hug, and team sources confirmed that there was a growing fear they've lost their young center for the foreseeable future.

The team did not have an official updated on Raynaud's injury after the game. He is expected to undergo an MRI late Saturday night. 

Raynaud made the All-Rookie second team last season after averaging 12.5 points and 7.5 rebounds in 74 games, proving to be a significant draft night find with the 42nd pick.

He was expected to play a key frontcourt role behind starting center Domantas Sabonis to open the season.

articles.headline: Vinícius Júnior 'sorry' after red card for hair pull; Mourinho skips Madrid presser
articles.description: Vinícius Júnior has apologized to his Real Madrid teammates and fans after being red-carded for pulling an opponent's hair in a dramatic, off-the-bench cameo during his team's LaLiga win over Villarreal on Saturday.
articles.headlineJa: ヴィニシウス・ジュニオール、髪を引っ張りレッドカードを受けたことを謝罪。ムリーニョは記者会見を欠席
articles.descriptionJa: 土曜日のラ・リーガ、ビジャレアル戦で勝利したレアル・マドリードのヴィニシウス・ジュニオールが、途中出場から相手選手の髪を引っ張ったことでレッドカードを受けた。彼はチームメイトとファンに謝罪した。
articles.body:
MADRID -- Vinícius Júnior has apologized to his Real Madrid teammates and fans after being red-carded for pulling an opponent's hair in a dramatic, off-the-bench cameo during his team's LaLiga win over Villarreal on Saturday.

Vinícius was celebrating scoring what he thought was Madrid's second goal when it was ruled out following a video review and he was instead sent off after replays showed he had pulled Nathan Saliba's hair in the build-up.

"The joy remains. Sorry to my team and the fans," Vinícius posted on Instagram following the game.

- Vinícius Júnior benched as Real Madrid take on Villarreal

- Atlético Madrid mock Real Madrid on social media over Federico Valverde recovery

- Kylian Mbappé to start for Real Madrid, criticism 'ridiculous' - José Mourinho

However, the decision sparked an angry reaction from the Madrid bench. Coach José Mourinho later skipped his scheduled post-match news conference.

The Brazil international was left out of the starting XI by Mourinho -- replaced by Yan Diomande -- after the coach admitted that the forward has been unable to find his best form this season.

Vinícius was introduced on 52 minutes with the game tied at 0-0, with Diomande opening the scoring at the Bernabéu 10 minutes later.

Vinícius then looked to have made a decisive contribution when he converted Jude Bellingham's pass to make it 2-0, with Mourinho sprinting onto the pitch to celebrate with his players.

However a VAR check showed he had pulled Saliba's hair as he raced forwards. The goal was overturned, and referee Isidro Díaz de Mera showed Vinícius a straight red card.

"I don't understand what's happening with the referees, with the red card. I don't understand it," midfielder Aurélien Tchouaméni told Real Madrid TV.

The referee's report said Vinicius had "disputed the [red card] decision, shouting, moving towards me with an aggressive attitude, and having to be restrained by his teammates."

Villarreal defender Juan Foyth had a different view of the incident.

"I don't think he meant to hurt anyone but it is a red card," the Argentina international said.

The star's punishment will be confirmed this week by the Spanish football federation's disciplinary panel, but Madrid have just one more league game -- against Sevilla on Oct. 18 -- before they travel to Barcelona for El Clásico on Oct. 25.

Although, the decision left 10-man Madrid to nervously defend a narrow lead in the game's closing stages, Mourinho's side saw out the 1-0 win.

The result leaves Real Madrid in third place in the LaLiga standings, a point behind Atlético Madrid and six points behind leaders Barcelona.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

articles.headline: Knicks' Towns opens up about grief for World Mental Health Day
articles.description: Karl-Anthony Towns shared his emotional journey following the death of his mother six years ago to mark World Mental Health Day on Saturday.
articles.headlineJa: ニックスのタウンズ、世界メンタルヘルスデーに際し喪失感について語る
articles.descriptionJa: カール＝アンソニー・タウンズは土曜日の世界メンタルヘルスデーに際し、6年前に母親を亡くした後の感情的な道のりについて明かした。
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- Karl-Anthony Towns has been traded from Minnesota, lost the conference finals and won the NBA title for his childhood team -- and still feels he is in the period of grief that began six years ago.

Just 10 days before the New York Knicks' banner-raising celebration, the All-Star big man marked World Mental Health Day by sharing his ongoing emotional journey following the death of his mother to complications from COVID-19.

Entering the first game of this year's NBA Finals, he said he felt "this very big calm" wash over him. He was taken back to amateur youth games with crowds so small he could spot his mom from anywhere.

"I felt like it was kind of just me, her and the game of basketball," he told the audience gathered Saturday by the nonprofit Project Healthy Minds. "I was able to be like an artist out there. I was able to have my paint brush and have a canvas with the court. And I was able to just paint a beautiful picture for her about the love I have for the game. The love I have to show the world because of her."

There was a time when he had lost that love for the game. Towns, whose bright smile became a constant image of the Knicks' championship run, said basketball "felt hollow" after his mother's death. "I didn't know if I wanted to do it anymore," he said.

But Towns found some solace in Arnie Kander, a well-known strength and wellness coach.

"Just to be heard, to be able to talk to someone you can trust, be able to really unload all that pain onto it and allow them to understand your feelings and articulate your feelings the right way, it makes life much lighter," he said. "And I felt myself getting lighter every time we kept talking."

Athletes embrace mental health Project Healthy Minds hopes Towns' example will inspire others to seek mental health care. The tech nonprofit runs a free online marketplace for finding therapy, psychiatry, support groups and other services. Its annual World Mental Health Day festival in New York offers an all-day schedule of yoga, art therapy and speakers.

Speaking Saturday with Towns was Boardroom CEO Rich Kleiman, the longtime manager for NBA superstar Kevin Durant and a new member of Project Healthy Minds' board.

Kleiman told The Associated Press that these sorts of conversations are growing more prevalent among athletes. DeMar DeRozan and Kevin Love kick-started the conversation eight years ago when DeRozan tweeted about depression and Love then published a first-person essay about anxiety. Kleiman recalled trading stories about anxiety attacks with Love for several hours one night shortly afterward.

Most players won't feel that comfortable constantly telling their story, Kleiman said. Mental health isn't a topic of discussion in the locker room. But he said players are certainly more aware of its impact.

"They just carry so much weight and speak to so many people," Kleiman told The Associated Press before the panel. "I think it says a lot that Karl Towns is feeling comfortable enou
